title: Psychedelic therapy: Will it be a game changer for mental health treatment? with Albert Garcia-Romeu, PhD

sentences.en: Before we get started today, I'd like to ask you to take a moment to fill out our listener survey.
sentences.zh: 在今天开始之前，我想请大家花点时间填写一下我们的听众调查问卷。

sentences.en: We'd like to know more about what you think of this podcast and what you'd like to see us do more of.
sentences.zh: 我们想更多地了解您对本播客的看法，以及您希望我们多做些什么内容。

sentences.en: We'd also like to know more about you.
sentences.zh: 我们也想更多地了解您。

sentences.en: So if you would, please go to our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org, and click on the link to our listener survey.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果您愿意的话，请访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org，并点击听众调查问卷的链接。

sentences.en: It should not take you long to complete.
sentences.zh: 完成它应该不会花您太长时间。

sentences.en: We'd really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们将不胜感激。

sentences.en: Now, on to the episode.
sentences.zh: 现在，进入本期节目。

sentences.en: We first talked about psychedelic therapy on this podcast three years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们三年前第一次在本播客中讨论了迷幻疗法。

sentences.en: Since then, interest in psychedelics has skyrocketed.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，人们对迷幻药的兴趣呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: Two states, Oregon and Colorado, have voted to legalize psilocybin use by adults.
sentences.zh: 俄勒冈州和科罗拉多州这两个州已经投票通过，将成年人使用裸盖菇素合法化。

sentences.en: And just last month, Australia became the first country in the world to recognize psychedelics as medicines.
sentences.zh: 就在上个月，澳大利亚成为世界上第一个承认迷幻药具有医疗用途的国家。

sentences.en: Doctors there will be able to prescribe psilocybin for depression and MDMA, popularly known as ecstasy or MOLLY, for post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 那里的医生将能够开具裸盖菇素用于治疗抑郁症，并开具 MDMA（俗称摇头丸或 MOLLY）用于治疗创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, researchers are studying psychedelic treatments for anxiety, addiction, and other behavioral health disorders.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，研究人员正在研究针对焦虑、成瘾和其他行为健康障碍的迷幻治疗方法。

sentences.en: So how did these drugs go from being a symbol of the 1960s counterculture to being touted as among the newest, most promising mental health treatments?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些药物是如何从 20 世纪 60 年代反主流文化的象征，变成被吹捧为最新、最有前景的心理健康治疗手段之一的呢？

sentences.en: And does the research back up the hype?
sentences.zh: 研究结果是否支持这些炒作？

sentences.en: How do psychedelics work in the brain?
sentences.zh: 迷幻药在大脑中是如何发挥作用的？

sentences.en: What have scientists found out about the types of mental health problems they can treat?
sentences.zh: 科学家们在它们可以治疗的心理健康问题类型方面发现了什么？

sentences.en: What's the legal status of these drugs?
sentences.zh: 这些药物的法律地位如何？

sentences.en: Are they likely to be approved as medications in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 它们在美国被批准为药物的可能性大吗？

sentences.en: And if they are, who will provide these treatments and who will have access to them?
sentences.zh: 如果获批，谁将提供这些治疗，谁又能获得这些治疗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Albert Garcia-Romeu, a psychologist and a member of the Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences faculty at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是 Albert Garcia-Romeu 博士，他是一位心理学家，也是约翰霍普金斯大学医学院精神病学和行为科学系的教员。

sentences.en: He is also a guest researcher at the National Institute on Drug Abuse.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是美国国家药物滥用研究所的客座研究员。

sentences.en: Dr. Garcia-Romeu studies the effects of psychedelic drugs in humans.
sentences.zh: Garcia-Romeu 博士研究迷幻药物对人类的影响。

sentences.en: His research interests include clinical applications of psychedelics, mindfulness and altered states of consciousness
sentences.zh: 他的研究兴趣包括迷幻药的临床应用、正念和意识改变状态，

sentences.en: and their underlying neurobiological mechanisms, as well as real-world drug use patterns and impacts on public health.
sentences.zh: 以及它们潜在的神经生物学机制，还有现实世界中的药物使用模式及其对公共卫生的影响。

sentences.en: He has also published dozens of research papers and has been widely interviewed in the media on psychedelic research.
sentences.zh: 他还发表了数十篇研究论文，并就迷幻药研究在媒体上接受过广泛采访。

sentences.en: Dr. Garcia-Romeu, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: Garcia-Romeu 博士，感谢您今天参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: I mentioned a couple of drugs in the introduction that our listeners have probably heard of, psilocybin and MDMA.
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中提到了两种听众可能听说过的药物：裸盖菇素和 MDMA。

sentences.en: How do you define a psychedelic?
sentences.zh: 您是如何定义迷幻药的？

sentences.en: What drugs does the term encompass?
sentences.zh: 这个术语涵盖了哪些药物？

sentences.en: Can you explain what each of them is and how they're similar and how they're different?
sentences.zh: 您能解释一下它们各自是什么，以及它们有何异同吗？

sentences.en: That's a lot of questions and I could teach a whole class about that, but we'll try to break it down into some of the basic components there.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的问题，我甚至可以为此开一门课，但我们会尝试将其拆解为一些基本组成部分来讲解。

sentences.en: The term psychedelic was actually coined by a psychiatrist named Humphrey Osmond back in 1957,
sentences.zh: “迷幻药”（psychedelic）这个词实际上是由一位名叫 Humphrey Osmond 的精神科医生在 1957 年创造的，

sentences.en: and he was interested in drugs like LSD and mescaline, which are what we call classic psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 他当时对 LSD 和麦司卡林等药物很感兴趣，这些就是我们所说的经典迷幻药。

sentences.en: They're serotonin-2A receptor agonist drugs.
sentences.zh: 它们是血清素 2A 受体激动剂药物。

sentences.en: And that's just pharmacologically the mechanism.
sentences.zh: 从药理学上讲，这就是它们的机制。

sentences.en: That's the way that they work in the brain as far as we can tell.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这就是它们在大脑中发挥作用的方式。

sentences.en: Psilocybin is another one of these classic psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 裸盖菇素是另一种经典迷幻药。

sentences.en: And so is DMT or dimethyltryptamine, which is found in the human brain as well as many plants and animals and is found in ayahuasca as well.
sentences.zh: DMT（二甲基色胺）也是如此，它存在于人脑以及许多动植物中，也存在于死藤水中。

sentences.en: And so there's this sort of canonical group of what we call classic psychedelics.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所说的经典迷幻药有一个典型的群体。

sentences.en: Most of those are naturally occurring.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数是天然存在的。

sentences.en: So, you know, I mentioned mescaline, which is found in peyote cactus and San Pedro cactus.
sentences.zh: 比如，我提到的麦司卡林，它存在于佩奥特仙人掌和圣佩德罗仙人掌中。

sentences.en: I've talked about DMT, which is found in different types of plants and animals.
sentences.zh: 我谈到了 DMT，它存在于不同类型的动植物中。

sentences.en: Also psilocybin, which is found in about 200 different species of mushrooms that grow all over the world.
sentences.zh: 还有裸盖菇素，它存在于全世界生长的约 200 种不同的蘑菇中。

sentences.en: And then, you know, LSD is sort of the semi-synthetic derivative that came out that was sort of, you know, brought the psychedelics into the limelight, if you will,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，LSD 是一种半合成衍生物，它让迷幻药进入了公众视野，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: during the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 是在 20 世纪期间。

sentences.en: And, you know, you mentioned the counterculture.
sentences.zh: 而且，你提到了反主流文化。

sentences.en: The LSD was definitely, you know, heavily involved in that period as well.
sentences.zh: LSD 在那个时期确实参与度很高。

sentences.en: And so that was something that was synthesized in the laboratory back in 1938 by a chemist named Dr. Albert Hoffman.
sentences.zh: 它是 1938 年由一位名叫 Albert Hoffman 的化学家在实验室中合成的。

sentences.en: But it works by the same mechanism as these other classic psychedelics, this serotonin-2A receptor mechanism.
sentences.zh: 但它的作用机制与其他经典迷幻药相同，即血清素 2A 受体机制。

sentences.en: And so we grouped those together.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将它们归为一类。

sentences.en: And when Osman was studying these drugs back in the 1950s, they were trying to find a better name for them because people were usually referring to them as psychotomimetics,
sentences.zh: 当 Osmond 在 20 世纪 50 年代研究这些药物时，他们试图为它们寻找一个更好的名字，因为人们通常称它们为“致精神病药”（psychotomimetics），

sentences.en: meaning that they seemed to mimic a psychotic state.
sentences.zh: 意思是它们似乎模仿了精神病状态。

sentences.en: And after working with these drugs and taking them himself, self-experimenting, he didn't feel that that was an accurate label.
sentences.zh: 在研究这些药物并亲自服用、进行自我实验后，他觉得这个标签并不准确。

sentences.en: He felt that there was more to the drug effects in that.
sentences.zh: 他认为这些药物的效果远不止于此。

sentences.en: And so he and the British author Humphrey Osman were actually going back and forth trying to figure out, you know,
sentences.zh: 于是，他和英国作家 Humphrey Osmond 实际上一直在反复讨论，试图弄清楚，你知道，

sentences.en: how do we call these drugs as more accurate representation of their effects?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何称呼这些药物，才能更准确地代表它们的效果？

sentences.en: And, you know, Huxley had famously written about his experience with mescaline in a book called The Doors of Perception.
sentences.zh: 赫胥黎（Huxley）曾在一本名为《知觉之门》（The Doors of Perception）的书中著名地写下了他使用麦司卡林的经历。

sentences.en: And eventually they landed on Osman proposed the word psychedelic because it was meant to characterize that this was a drug that was sort of uncovering something that was in the psyche.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们确定了 Osmond 提议的词“psychedelic”，因为它旨在表征这是一种揭示心灵深处某种东西的药物。

sentences.en: It was allowing something in the psyche to manifest or to be revealed.
sentences.zh: 它允许心灵中的某些东西显现或被揭示出来。

sentences.en: And that was his, you know, using the Greek terminology to sort of come up with a new label.
sentences.zh: 这就是他利用希腊语词源来构思一个新标签的过程。

sentences.en: And that really is the beginning of that term specifically back in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 这确实是该术语在 20 世纪 50 年代的起源。

sentences.en: However, you know, since then the word psychedelic has been used in so many different ways to talk about artwork, to talk about music, to talk about culture.
sentences.zh: 然而，自那时起，“迷幻”这个词被以各种方式使用，用来谈论艺术作品、音乐和文化。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the very strict sort of pharmacological classification is not always the way that people talk about these drugs in real life.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常严格的药理学分类并不总是人们在现实生活中谈论这些药物的方式。

sentences.en: And certainly MDMA and even cannabis at times have been sort of lumped in with these psychedelics or drugs that can cause psychedelic-like states, whatever that means.
sentences.zh: 当然，MDMA 甚至大麻有时也被归入这些迷幻药，或者被归为能引起类似迷幻状态的药物，无论这意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so MDMA, although it's not exactly the same from a pharmacological standpoint as some of these other classic psychedelics,
sentences.zh: 所以 MDMA，虽然从药理学角度来看它与某些经典迷幻药不完全相同，

sentences.en: it does induce a really strong altered state of consciousness, which is one of these key factors that people look at in terms of creating what you'd consider a psychedelic effect.
sentences.zh: 但它确实能诱导一种非常强烈的意识改变状态，这是人们在考虑创造所谓的“迷幻效果”时关注的关键因素之一。

sentences.en: And so people often talk about MDMA as a psychedelic, though it's also been talked about as being an intactogen, for instance,
sentences.zh: 因此，人们经常把 MDMA 称为迷幻药，尽管它也被称为“移情药”（entactogen），例如，

sentences.en: which means it allows a person to access what's within their mind and their emotional states.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它允许一个人接触到他们内心深处和情绪状态。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's lots of different ways that we talk about these.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们谈论这些药物的方式有很多种。

sentences.en: And even now, scientists, myself included, are going back and forth talking about, you know, what does psychedelic really mean and what is the definition of psychedelic medicine?
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，科学家们（包括我自己）也在反复讨论，“迷幻”到底意味着什么？迷幻医学的定义又是什么？

sentences.en: So it's an interesting time because the field, I think, is coming back to grapple with some of this, you know, these terms and what do they mean?
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的时期，因为我认为该领域正在重新审视这些术语及其含义。

sentences.en: What about the drug ketamine?
sentences.zh: 那氯胺酮（ketamine）呢？

sentences.en: It's often lumped into the psychedelic category, and it's the only one of these drugs that's FDA approved and people can get a prescription for right now.
sentences.zh: 它经常被归入迷幻药类别，而且它是目前唯一获得 FDA 批准且人们可以获得处方的药物。

sentences.en: Is ketamine a psychedelic?
sentences.zh: 氯胺酮是迷幻药吗？

sentences.en: So ketamine is a slightly different drug.
sentences.zh: 氯胺酮是一种略有不同的药物。

sentences.en: It's what we, I would call it a dissociative anesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我会称它为一种解离性麻醉剂。

sentences.en: It's been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 它已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: We use it for anesthesia, you know, in medicine, both animals and humans all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们在医学上一直用它作为麻醉剂，无论是对动物还是人类。

sentences.en: It's pretty common place.
sentences.zh: 它非常普遍。

sentences.en: But when you use a sub-anesthetic dose, basically a dose that doesn't knock a person out, they can also have these psychedelic-like states,
sentences.zh: 但当你使用亚麻醉剂量时，也就是不会让人失去知觉的剂量，人们也会产生这些类似迷幻的状态，

sentences.en: which include feelings of being outside of one's body and having different types of altered states of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 包括感觉自己脱离了身体，并拥有不同类型的意识改变状态。

sentences.en: And, again, when you're talking really broadly about a drug that can create an altered state, that's usually the sort of loose usage of that word psychedelic.
sentences.zh: 同样，当你非常广泛地谈论一种可以创造改变状态的药物时，这通常就是“迷幻”这个词的松散用法。

sentences.en: And so people talk about doing, for instance, psychedelic therapy using ketamine.
sentences.zh: 所以人们谈论使用氯胺酮进行迷幻疗法。

sentences.en: But when you're doing that, you know, again, the pharmacological mechanisms are slightly different than they are from the classic psychedelics or from MDMA.
sentences.zh: 但当你这样做时，药理机制与经典迷幻药或 MDMA 略有不同。

sentences.en: So is ketamine operating on the same part of the brain or someplace different in the brain?
sentences.zh: 那么氯胺酮是作用于大脑的同一部分，还是大脑的其他部位？

sentences.en: Well, the mechanism behind the drug action is more rooted in the glutamatergic system and the specific NMDA receptors that are part of the glutamate system.
sentences.zh: 药物作用背后的机制更多地植根于谷氨酸能系统和作为谷氨酸系统一部分的特定 NMDA 受体。

sentences.en: So we know that that seems to be one of the targets for these drugs that's slightly different from the classic psychedelics that work more in the serotonin system.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，这似乎是这些药物的目标之一，与更多作用于血清素系统的经典迷幻药略有不同。

sentences.en: But ultimately, you know, we're talking about the same brain and the same brain networks, and they end up having quite a bit of overlap, it seems,
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我们谈论的是同一个大脑和同一个大脑网络，它们似乎有相当多的重叠，

sentences.en: in terms of the type of effects that people are experiencing when they're under the influence.
sentences.zh: 就人们在药物影响下所经历的效果类型而言。

sentences.en: And so, for instance,
sentences.zh: 例如，

sentences.en: one of the types of experiences that people often will talk about when they have either sub-anesthetic ketamine dosing or dosing with the classic psychedelic is this unit of state,
sentences.zh: 当人们进行亚麻醉剂量的氯胺酮给药或经典迷幻药给药时，经常谈论的一种体验就是这种“统一状态”，

sentences.en: this feeling of the boundaries between self and other sort of coming down and feeling more interconnected with the world.
sentences.zh: 这种自我与他人之间的界限感消失，并感到与世界更加互联的感觉。

sentences.en: And those types of experiences can be occasioned both by the classic psychedelics, but as well as ketamine and other types of practices like meditation and so forth.
sentences.zh: 这些类型的体验既可以由经典迷幻药引起，也可以由氯胺酮以及冥想等其他类型的练习引起。

sentences.en: Has the huge uptick in public interest in psychedelics over the past few years come as a surprise to you?
sentences.zh: 过去几年公众对迷幻药的兴趣激增，这让你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: And has doing work in this area changed over the last decade?
sentences.zh: 在这一领域开展工作在过去十年中发生了变化吗？

sentences.en: So I would say yes.
sentences.zh: 我会说是的。

sentences.en: You know, I think it's been a little bit surprising to see how enthusiastic popular culture has become about all the work that's happening in this field and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为看到大众文化对该领域正在进行的所有工作表现出如此热情，确实有点令人惊讶，而且，

sentences.en: the prospects of psychedelic therapies.
sentences.zh: 迷幻疗法的前景也是如此。

sentences.en: I think, you know, many people would have said 10 years ago that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想，10 年前很多人会说，

sentences.en: they would have been skeptical about sort of widespread adoption of this type of treatment in a medical setting.
sentences.zh: 他们会对这种治疗方法在医疗环境中的广泛采用持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: And nowadays, it seems almost imminent and actually with MDMA, we will be seeing that in practice, you know, in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而如今，这似乎迫在眉睫，实际上对于 MDMA，我们最早将在明年就能在美国看到它在实践中应用。

sentences.en: as early as next year.
sentences.zh: 正如你提到的，氯胺酮已经可以使用了，而且人们对以这种方式使用氯胺酮的兴趣日益浓厚，因为这并不是一种曾经被广泛实践的治疗方式，

sentences.en: And then, as you mentioned, ketamine is already available and there is a growing interest in using ketamine in this way because it's not something that had been practiced,
sentences.zh: 你知道，进行这种类型的氯胺酮治疗。

sentences.en: you know, in a widespread fashion to be doing this type of ketamine therapy.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，人们对这类事物的兴趣和市场才开始增长。

sentences.en: Only until recently did there become, again, growing interest in market for something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你看到了提供这些服务的公司在不断壮大。

sentences.en: And so now you're seeing the growth of that to provide those types of services from different companies out there.
sentences.zh: 那么迷幻药可以治疗哪些精神障碍？

sentences.en: So what are the mental disorders that psychedelics can treat?
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到澳大利亚批准了针对抑郁症和创伤后应激障碍的治疗。

sentences.en: I mentioned in the intro that Australia approved treatments for depression and post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 这是目前证据最充分的领域吗？

sentences.en: Is that where the evidence is the strongest at this point?
sentences.zh: 是的，有很多工作始于 20 世纪 50 年代和 60 年代的经典迷幻药研究。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's been a lot of work that sort of started, again, with the classic psychedelics back in the 1950s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 你看到了相当多的研究。

sentences.en: You saw a good amount of research.
sentences.zh: 然后在 20 世纪 70 年代遭到抵制和定罪后，研究一度沉寂了一段时间。

sentences.en: Then that sort of died down for some time after backlash and criminalization in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，自 90 年代末、2000 年代初以来，你开始看到研究再次回升。

sentences.en: But really, since the late 90s, early 2000s, you start to see another uptick in research.
sentences.zh: 是的，你提到了几种不同的疾病。

sentences.en: And, yeah, you noted a couple of different conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以那些非常接近获批的，例如 MDMA，就是将 MDMA 与谈话疗法结合用于治疗创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。

sentences.en: So the ones that are very close to approval for, for instance, MDMA is use of MDMA with talk therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder, PTSD.
sentences.zh: 这实际上已经完成了两项三期临床试验，由多学科迷幻研究协会（MAPS）赞助。

sentences.en: And so that's actually undergone two phase three clinical trials now that were sponsored by the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies, MAPS.
sentences.zh: 在这两项研究中，尽管第二项研究尚未发表，但结果非常积极。

sentences.en: And in both of those studies, although the second study has not yet been published, the results have been overwhelmingly positive.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，在参与研究的人群中，症状得到了很大程度的缓解，心理健康状况也有所改善。

sentences.en: And they found a lot of remission of symptoms and improvement in mental health status in these folks who were going through the study.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们在 12 周的治疗过程中接受了三次 MDMA 给药。

sentences.en: They're getting, I believe it was three doses of MDMA during the course of treatment, which lasts about 12 weeks.
sentences.zh: 在药物给药前后都有准备工作。

sentences.en: And there's preparation before and after the drug is administered.
sentences.zh: 而且，在中间的几周里，通常会进行不同类型的咨询或谈话疗法。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the intervening weeks, there's often different types of counseling or talk therapy going on.
sentences.zh: 与安慰剂组相比，接受这些治疗的人表现出了更高的反应率。

sentences.en: And the people who are getting those types of treatments versus placebo are showing a far greater response rate.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到大多数接受 MDMA 治疗 PTSD 的人，其改善程度远超仅进行谈话疗法所能达到的效果。

sentences.en: And so you're seeing a majority of people who get that MDMA therapy with PTSD are improving above and beyond what they would be doing with just the talk therapy alone.
sentences.zh: 这就是为了获得 FDA 医疗批准所必需的数据类型。

sentences.en: And so those are the types of data that are necessary in order to get a medical approval through the FDA.
sentences.zh: 目前来看，对于 MDMA 来说，这确实非常接近了。

sentences.en: And at this point, you see that is, again, very close with MDMA.
sentences.zh: 所以到明年，看起来 MDMA 的分类将会发生变化。

sentences.en: And so by next year, it's seeming as though you're going to see a change in the classification of MDMA.
sentences.zh: 它不再被视为一级管制药物，而是可以由希望用它来帮助 PTSD 患者的医生和临床医生开具处方。

sentences.en: So it's no longer considered Schedule I, but it can be prescribed by physicians and clinicians who want to use it to help people with PTSD.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我认为目前 MDMA 疗法的大部分证据所集中的地方。

sentences.en: And, yeah, that's where I would say most of the evidence with MDMA therapy has been focused so far.
sentences.zh: 其他人正在研究 MDMA 在治疗物质使用障碍或其他类型的心理健康状况方面的应用。

sentences.en: Other folks are working on looking at MDMA and treating things like substance use disorders or other types of mental health conditions.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，PTSD 一直是重头戏。

sentences.en: But so far, yeah, PTSD has been the big one.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果一个人为了治疗物质使用障碍而服用 MDMA，他们的大脑中发生了什么？

sentences.en: So what's happening in people's brains, say, if you're taking MDMA for a substance use disorder?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么这比目前市面上的其他治疗方法更有效？

sentences.en: I mean, why would that work as opposed to any of the other treatments that are out there right now?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这与戒酒硫（Antabuse）之类的药物有什么区别？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the difference between that and, say, antabuse?
sentences.zh: 嗯，戒酒硫绝对不是那种耐受性良好的药物。

sentences.en: Well, antabuse is definitely not one of these drugs that's well-tolerated.
sentences.zh: 人们通常不喜欢使用它，因为如果他们想喝酒，他们就会停止服用这种药。

sentences.en: People don't usually like to use it because, you know, if they just if they want to drink, then they just stop taking the medicine.
sentences.zh: 而且，物质使用障碍的类型有很多，治疗方法也各不相同。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's lots of different types of substance use disorders and treatments for those that vary widely.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些迷幻疗法的独特之处在于，通常通过一个疗程的谈话疗法，并在几个月内进行一到三次药物给药，

sentences.en: But what I think sets apart these psychedelic therapies is that usually with a course of talk therapy and somewhere in between one and three drug administrations over the course of a few months,
sentences.zh: 你通常能够帮助人们超越不仅仅是问题行为（例如酒精或药物使用），

sentences.en: you're usually able to help people move beyond sort of not just the problematic behavior, which would be, for instance, you know, alcohol or drug use,
sentences.zh: 而且往往能触及问题的根源，

sentences.en: but often to kind of get to the root of the issue,
sentences.zh: 从心理上解决一些与他们最初使用这些物质的原因相关的潜在问题。

sentences.en: to psychologically work through some of the presenting problems that are related to the reasons why they use those substances to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为许多当前的治疗方法侧重于掩盖戒断或渴望等症状，或者试图让人们在表面上避免使用药物。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of current treatments are focused on masking things like withdrawal or craving or trying to keep people so that they're able to avoid using the drug sort of on a very surface level.
sentences.zh: 但当你开始深入挖掘他们产生这些行为的根源时，你就能真正做出长期持久的改变。

sentences.en: But when you start to go down into the deeper roots of why it is that they're doing those types of behaviors, then you're able to really make long-term lasting changes.
sentences.zh: 至于他们在大脑中做了什么，我认为这仍然是一个巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: In terms of, you know, what are they doing in the brain, that's still really a big mystery, I would say.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年左右的时间里，我们看到了更多关于迷幻药和 MDMA 的研究，以了解它们的大脑机制。

sentences.en: We've seen a lot more research over the last decade or so looking at psychedelics and MDMA to understand their brain mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上仍在解析这些机制，并试图区分不同类型的药物在做什么，以及为什么它们会产生那样的影响，

sentences.en: But we're really still unpacking those and trying to differentiate what the different types of drugs are doing and why they have the impact that they do,
sentences.zh: 这意味着你看到了长期的变化，包括几个月后人们仍然表现出改善。

sentences.en: meaning that you're seeing long-term changes, including things like, you know, months later, people are still showing improvements,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的长期疗效。

sentences.en: which is not the case with a drug like Antibus, for instance, or like SSRI, standard antidepressant, because when you stop taking those, then they stop working.
sentences.zh: 例如像安他布（Antibus）或SSRIs这类标准抗抑郁药就并非如此，因为一旦你停止服用，它们就不再起作用了。

sentences.en: How much is known about how these drugs are helping people where other treatments don't, for example, using psilocybin to treat persistent depression?
sentences.zh: 对于这些药物如何在其他疗法无效的情况下帮助患者，比如使用裸盖菇素治疗持续性抑郁症，目前了解多少？

sentences.en: So, that's actually an area that's been an active study, and particularly with psilocybin, as you noted,
sentences.zh: 这是一个目前正在积极研究的领域，正如你所提到的，特别是针对裸盖菇素的研究，

sentences.en: you know, that's well far along in terms of studying that as an antidepressant treatment,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在将其作为抗抑郁治疗手段的研究方面，已经取得了相当大的进展，

sentences.en: both in people with major depression, but also in people with treatment-resistant major depression,
sentences.zh: 不仅针对重度抑郁症患者，也针对那些难治性重度抑郁症患者，

sentences.en: which is a person who's failed multiple different, you know, failed to improve after taking multiple different types of treatments or medications.
sentences.zh: 也就是指那些尝试过多种不同治疗方法或药物后，病情仍未好转的人。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, those cases, you know, are usually thought of as being a little more serious
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这些病例通常被认为稍微严重一些，

sentences.en: because people are not responding to the traditional therapies and treatments that are available.
sentences.zh: 因为患者对现有的传统疗法和治疗手段没有反应。

sentences.en: And so, in those cases, what they found is that, you know, in a nice large study that was published, this is actually the biggest study published on psilocybin so far,
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些病例中，他们发现，在一项已发表的规模较大的研究中——这实际上是迄今为止关于裸盖菇素规模最大的研究——

sentences.en: and it was about 230 people or so with treatment-resistant depression, and they either got one high dose of psilocybin, which is 25 milligrams,
sentences.zh: 大约有230名难治性抑郁症患者参与，他们要么接受了一次25毫克的高剂量裸盖菇素治疗，

sentences.en: or they got 10 milligrams of psilocybin, which is a moderately low dose, or they got a placebo-like dose of one milligram of psilocybin that usually doesn't have much of an effect.
sentences.zh: 要么接受了10毫克的中低剂量，或者接受了1毫克几乎没有效果的安慰剂剂量。

sentences.en: And they were able to see that the people who got that single high dose were showing improvements in their depression.
sentences.zh: 他们观察到，接受单次高剂量治疗的患者，其抑郁症状有所改善。

sentences.en: On average, it lasted out to three weeks after the drug.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，这种效果在用药后持续了三周。

sentences.en: And again, that's, you know, first, different in a couple of ways from our standard treatments.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这与我们的标准治疗方式在几个方面有所不同。

sentences.en: First, you know, those people are getting symptom improvements immediately after they've gotten the drug dose,
sentences.zh: 首先，这些患者在接受药物剂量后，症状立即得到了改善，

sentences.en: and that's different than a lot of our standard antidepressant medicines that usually take weeks to start working.
sentences.zh: 这与我们许多通常需要数周才能起效的标准抗抑郁药物不同。

sentences.en: And the other thing is, these are people who had already failed to respond to other types of medications,
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，这些患者之前已经对其他类型的药物治疗没有反应，

sentences.en: and yet they are still seeing these improvements in their depression that last weeks after the single dosing.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然在单次给药后，看到了持续数周的抑郁症状改善。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's not even taking into account other studies like ours here at Hopkins,
sentences.zh: 而且，这还没算上我们霍普金斯大学（Hopkins）等机构的其他研究，

sentences.en: where people got two doses and are showing symptom remission and improvements that last up to a year later.
sentences.zh: 在那些研究中，人们接受了两次给药，并表现出症状缓解和持续长达一年的改善。

sentences.en: And so, really, that is exciting because for a lot of people who are not responding to current treatments, you know, we need something new.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实令人兴奋，因为对于许多对现有疗法没有反应的人来说，我们需要新的东西。

sentences.en: We need something that works better.
sentences.zh: 我们需要效果更好的疗法。

sentences.en: And the idea that you could take one or a few doses of this drug and, you know,
sentences.zh: 而这种只需服用一剂或几剂药物，

sentences.en: supplement that with some talk therapy and see these long-lasting benefits is, in many ways, revolutionary for the field.
sentences.zh: 并辅以心理谈话疗法就能获得长期疗效的想法，在许多方面对该领域来说都是革命性的。

sentences.en: Are there certain people who should not take psychedelics for problems that they have?
sentences.zh: 是否有些人不应该为了解决自身问题而使用迷幻药？

sentences.en: For example, I've read that these drugs could be harmful to people with bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 例如，我读到过这些药物可能对双相情感障碍患者有害。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么？

sentences.en: There's concerns, and there have been case studies and other data from people who have used these psychedelics out in the world
sentences.zh: 确实存在担忧，并且有一些案例研究和其他数据表明，在现实世界中使用过这些迷幻药的人，

sentences.en: who have then gone on to develop manic symptoms, you know, and that obviously can be problematic.
sentences.zh: 后来出现了躁狂症状，这显然是有问题的。

sentences.en: We don't want to, you know, put anyone on a course where their mental health status is going to deteriorate after you give them a high dose of the drug.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让任何人在服用高剂量药物后，心理健康状况反而恶化。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that's been one area where people have been very careful in excluding folks who have bipolar mood.
sentences.zh: 所以，在排除双相情感障碍患者方面，人们一直非常谨慎。

sentences.en: However, there are preliminary data showing that people who get psilocybin who have a milder form of bipolar mood seem to respond well and have not seen these incidents of mania.
sentences.zh: 然而，初步数据显示，患有较轻微双相情感障碍的人在服用裸盖菇素后似乎反应良好，并没有出现躁狂的情况。

sentences.en: However, you still get the case reports from people out in the community who have had those types of situations.
sentences.zh: 不过，你仍然会从社区中听到那些出现过此类情况的病例报告。

sentences.en: And so, obviously, it's still an open question, and it's an area that I think requires more study.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题，我认为这是一个需要更多研究的领域。

sentences.en: The main area that we know that, you know, people who receive high-dose psychedelics may have lasting problems afterwards
sentences.zh: 我们已知的主要领域是，接受高剂量迷幻药的人可能会在事后产生持久的问题，

sentences.en: would be people who have a predisposition to psychotic illness, schizophrenia, those types of conditions.
sentences.zh: 那就是有精神病倾向的人，比如精神分裂症或其他此类疾病的患者。

sentences.en: If they either have a personal or family history of one of those disorders or if they've, you know, had symptoms of that type of condition,
sentences.zh: 如果他们本人或家族有此类疾病史，或者如果他们曾经出现过此类症状，

sentences.en: we would often screen those people out of our research studies, mainly because you would be, again,
sentences.zh: 我们通常会将这些人排除在研究之外，主要是因为你必须，再次强调，

sentences.en: trying to avoid precipitating ongoing problems, including things like psychotic symptoms that can last, you know,
sentences.zh: 尽量避免诱发持续性的问题，包括像精神病症状这类可能持续，你知道，

sentences.en: for months or longer if, you know, things don't go the way that we want them to.
sentences.zh: 数月甚至更久的问题，如果事情没有按照我们预期的方向发展的话。

sentences.en: Some of the people who are listening to this may themselves be experiencing some syndromes where they think that these kinds of drugs might be helpful to them.
sentences.zh: 一些正在收听节目的听众可能自己正经历着某些综合征，并认为这些药物可能对他们有帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, where does the average person go to participate?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，普通人去哪里参与研究呢？

sentences.en: Say, it's got to be a clinical trial at this point, right?
sentences.zh: 目前肯定得是临床试验，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, because most of this stuff is not approved for general use.
sentences.zh: 因为这些东西大多还没有被批准用于一般用途。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, there are many people who are trying to self-treat or to find treatment underground.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，有很多人试图进行自我治疗或在地下渠道寻找治疗方法。

sentences.en: That, you know, even in places where legalization or decriminalization might have occurred, you know, that's still illegal at the federal level.
sentences.zh: 即使在某些已经实现合法化或非刑事化的地方，这在联邦层面仍然是非法的。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are penalties for that, criminal penalties and other things that can happen that are problematic.
sentences.zh: 所以，这会带来刑事处罚和其他可能发生的麻烦，这些都是问题。

sentences.en: But in terms of, you know, finding something legally available in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但就如何在美国合法获得这些治疗而言，

sentences.en: particularly, yeah, you would want to go to a website called clinicaltrials.gov.
sentences.zh: 特别是，你得去一个叫 clinicaltrials.gov 的网站。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, a registry where all the clinical trials that are happening both here and abroad are, you know, listed out.
sentences.zh: 那是一个注册中心，列出了国内外正在进行的所有临床试验。

sentences.en: You can look by condition.
sentences.zh: 你可以按疾病种类搜索。

sentences.en: You can look by keywords such as psilocybin, for instance.
sentences.zh: 你可以按关键词搜索，比如“裸盖菇素”。

sentences.en: You can look by location and try to find things that are available.
sentences.zh: 你可以按地点搜索，尝试找到可用的项目。

sentences.en: I would say even though the work is growing, there's still just a few hub regions where you can get a lot of research happening.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，尽管相关研究正在增加，但目前能进行大量研究的中心区域仍然很少。

sentences.en: And otherwise, you know, there's a lot of folks who not necessarily have access because either the work is not happening near them
sentences.zh: 否则，很多人未必能获得参与机会，因为要么研究不在他们附近进行，

sentences.en: or the clinical trials inclusion criteria are very strict, which they tend to be, you know, primarily for safety's sake.
sentences.zh: 要么临床试验的纳入标准非常严格，这通常主要是为了安全起见。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So what's the outlook for these drugs being approved as medications in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些药物在美国被批准为药物的前景如何？

sentences.en: You mentioned MDMA seems close, but what about psilocybin?
sentences.zh: 你提到MDMA似乎快要获批了，那裸盖菇素呢？

sentences.en: What about some of the others that you mentioned, DMT that comes from ayahuasca, things like that?
sentences.zh: 还有你提到的其他药物，比如来自死藤水的DMT，诸如此类的东西呢？

sentences.en: Well, psilocybin is probably the next closest to approval, I would say,
sentences.zh: 嗯，裸盖菇素可能是下一个最接近获批的，我想说，

sentences.en: because there's been such a preponderance of research looking at it for depression and then also for other conditions like substance use and existential distress.
sentences.zh: 因为已经有大量的研究在探讨它对抑郁症以及物质使用障碍和存在主义困境等其他疾病的疗效。

sentences.en: And so my forecast, if you will, would be that, you know, within the next three or four years,
sentences.zh: 所以我的预测是，在未来三到四年内，

sentences.en: you'll likely see psilocybin getting into that approval process with the FDA as a new treatment,
sentences.zh: 你很可能会看到裸盖菇素进入FDA的新药审批流程，

sentences.en: something that will be then accessible to people who are able to get psilocybin treatment by a licensed clinician,
sentences.zh: 届时，那些能够通过执业临床医生获得裸盖菇素治疗的人将能使用它，

sentences.en: particularly for things like major depression, which is where, again, a lot of the data have been so far.
sentences.zh: 特别是针对重度抑郁症等疾病，这也是目前数据最集中的领域。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of widespread study right now of other types of psychedelics, LSD, mescaline, DMT.
sentences.zh: 目前对于其他类型的迷幻药，如LSD、麦司卡林、DMT，还没有广泛的研究。

sentences.en: There's been small studies here and there.
sentences.zh: 只有零星的小规模研究。

sentences.en: The regulatory red tape to do this work and then also the sort of regular or typical form of medication approval in this country,
sentences.zh: 进行这项工作的监管繁文缛节，以及这个国家常规的药物审批形式，

sentences.en: you know, kind of make it difficult to do this work because between the regulatory approvals and hurdles that we have to get jumped through to do this,
sentences.zh: 使得这项工作很难开展，因为在监管审批和我们必须跨越的障碍之间，

sentences.en: the enormous cost of doing the research.
sentences.zh: 研究成本极其高昂。

sentences.en: And then if you're talking about something like LSD, for instance, that's not a patentable molecule because it's been around for so long,
sentences.zh: 而且如果你谈论的是像LSD这样的药物，由于它存在已久，无法申请专利，

sentences.en: then it makes it quite difficult to move it through this process and to get people to invest in that because,
sentences.zh: 那么要推动它走完这个流程并吸引投资就变得非常困难，因为，

sentences.en: oh, why would anyone spend money to study it if they can't get a return on investment from a capitalist standpoint?
sentences.zh: 哦，如果从资本的角度无法获得投资回报，为什么还会有人花钱去研究它呢？

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So those are the drug manufacturers, the ones who have the money to go through the process.
sentences.zh: 所以那些是制药商，他们才有钱去走完这个流程。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, you know, since they don't own those molecules and they don't feel compelled to study them.
sentences.zh: 但是，由于他们不拥有这些分子的专利，他们也就没有动力去研究它们。

sentences.en: And so that's why you've seen such a long process with something like MDMA or psilocybin,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么像MDMA或裸盖菇素这样的药物经历了如此漫长的过程，

sentences.en: where the funding to do this research has sort of come in piecemeal over the course of literally decades to get it to where we're at with the science.
sentences.zh: 研究资金在过去几十年里断断续续地投入，才有了我们今天所看到的科学成果。

sentences.en: Now, you've written about equity and access issues, both in terms of who is being included in the research trials on these drugs,
sentences.zh: 你曾撰文讨论过公平性和获取渠道的问题，既包括谁被纳入了这些药物的临床试验，

sentences.en: but also who might have access to the treatments eventually.
sentences.zh: 也包括最终谁能获得这些治疗。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, it's been pointed out that many of the research studies that have been published
sentences.zh: 嗯，有人指出，许多已发表的关于MDMA或裸盖菇素的研究，

sentences.en: using MDMA or psilocybin have been predominantly white, predominantly high socioeconomic status participants.
sentences.zh: 其参与者主要是白人，且多为高社会经济地位人群。

sentences.en: And there's a number of structural reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有许多结构性原因。

sentences.en: And then there's a number of cultural reasons for that as well, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有许多文化层面的原因。

sentences.en: But we'll say I think it's over 85 percent of participants in the clinical trials that to date have occurred using psilocybin and MDMA have been white.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，迄今为止，参与裸盖菇素和MDMA临床试验的参与者中，超过85%是白人。

sentences.en: And if you want to kind of think about why is that, you know, some of those structural reasons that I mentioned include things,
sentences.zh: 如果你想思考为什么会这样，我提到的那些结构性原因包括一些因素，

sentences.en: factors such as just not being able to get off of work to spend a whole day in a therapy session like this and, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如无法请假去花一整天时间进行这样的治疗，你知道，

sentences.en: being able to do that multiple times or not being able to get away from child care or domestic issues that have to be taken care of.
sentences.zh: 无法多次这样做，或者无法摆脱育儿或必须处理的家庭琐事。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's one thing that I think is really skewed this work in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是导致这项工作在某种程度上出现偏差的一个原因。

sentences.en: Culturally, I also think that there's a lot of mistrust of the medical institutions and biomedical research for a number of reasons,
sentences.zh: 在文化上，我也认为由于种种原因，人们对医疗机构和生物医学研究存在很多不信任，

sentences.en: historic abuses, things of that nature that, you know, I think make people mistrustful of coming to do a study where you're going to take a drug that if you,
sentences.zh: 历史上的滥用行为等等，我认为这让人们对参加一项需要服用药物的研究感到不信任，如果你，

sentences.en: you know, have read popular media, you might think, well, this drug might make me go crazy or this drug, you know, is going to make me feel really strange.
sentences.zh: 读过大众媒体的报道，你可能会想，这种药会不会让我发疯，或者这种药会让我感觉非常奇怪。

sentences.en: And I don't know who, you know, who's going to be around me or what's going to happen or what are they going to do to me?
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁会在我身边，会发生什么，或者他们会对我不利吗？

sentences.en: And so I think that can be a really very real concern for people, not to mention, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这对人们来说是一个非常现实的担忧，更不用说，

sentences.en: the years and years of criminalization and stigmatization of drugs and drug use in general that make people probably raise an eyebrow and say,
sentences.zh: 多年来对药物和药物使用的刑事化和污名化，让人们可能会挑起眉毛说，

sentences.en: you know, they want to take me into a laboratory and give me this illegal drug.
sentences.zh: 他们想把我带进实验室，给我服用这种非法药物。

sentences.en: I don't know if I'm comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否能接受。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think that's a big problem with psychedelic research to this point is that it has been predominantly white,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是目前迷幻药研究的一个大问题，即参与者主要是白人，

sentences.en: predominantly higher socioeconomic status participants.
sentences.zh: 主要是较高社会经济地位的人群。

sentences.en: But, you know, this is something that actually, you know, is parallel in all sorts of biomedical research.
sentences.zh: 但是，这其实在各类生物医学研究中都是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: And so it does point to these bigger problems, which is, you know, you see less than 5% of people who are in trials of new FDA-approved medications,
sentences.zh: 这指向了更大的问题，即在90年代和2000年代，FDA批准的新药临床试验中，

sentences.en: you know, in the 90s and 2000s were coming from Black, African-American, Hispanic backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 黑人、非裔美国人、西班牙裔背景的参与者比例不到5%。

sentences.en: And so you're seeing, again, a very homogeneous population in many of these studies for any sort of medical research.
sentences.zh: 所以，在任何类型的医学研究中，你都会看到这些研究的人群非常单一。

sentences.en: And that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题。

sentences.en: And the other problem, I think, at another level is that many of the researchers themselves are not representative of the broader community.
sentences.zh: 另一个层面的问题是，许多研究人员本身也无法代表更广泛的社区。

sentences.en: And so you see less than 5% of the researchers doing these studies are coming from a Black, African-American, Hispanic, indigenous background.
sentences.zh: 进行这些研究的研究人员中，黑人、非裔美国人、西班牙裔、原住民背景的比例不到5%。

sentences.en: And so that also, I think, would make people hesitant to necessarily want to come in and feel invested to do this type of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这也会让人们在想要参与并投入这类研究时感到犹豫。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's, I think, many different layers there to be unpacked.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这里面有很多不同的层面需要去剖析。

sentences.en: But ultimately, you know, I'm hoping that both the researchers and the participants are able to diversify over the next decade.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我希望在未来十年里，研究人员和参与者都能实现多元化。

sentences.en: And that also, you know, should this type of treatment be approved soon, that we're going to find ways to make that available and accessible to people,
sentences.zh: 而且，如果这类治疗很快获批，我们应该找到方法让它变得可用且易于获取，

sentences.en: particularly people who are coming from lower SES backgrounds,
sentences.zh: 特别是对于那些来自较低社会经济背景的人来说，

sentences.en: because they often have big health disparities and issues that they need to deal with that include many of the types of problems that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 因为他们往往面临巨大的健康差距和问题，需要处理包括我们正在讨论的许多问题。

sentences.en: Post-traumatic stress, substance use, depression, and so on.
sentences.zh: 创伤后应激障碍、物质使用、抑郁症等等。

sentences.en: Oh, that all makes sense.
sentences.zh: 哦，这些都说得通。

sentences.en: I want to change gears a little bit and talk about microdosing, which is taking small amounts of some of these drugs on a regular basis to treat a variety of issues.
sentences.zh: 我想换个话题，谈谈微剂量给药，也就是定期服用少量这些药物来治疗各种问题。

sentences.en: Now, proponents say that taking tiny doses of psychedelics that are too small to have real psychedelic effects can help with mood, creativity, productivity,
sentences.zh: 支持者称，服用剂量极小、不足以产生真正迷幻效果的迷幻药，可以改善情绪、创造力、生产力，

sentences.en: and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 以及各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: Is there any research that backs this up?
sentences.zh: 有任何研究支持这一点吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: Um, so there haven't, well, and the, you know, I should say there's not really a lot of research to begin with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，并没有，而且，你知道，我应该说，本来就没有多少研究。

sentences.en: Um, most of what we have is anecdotal and you can collect anecdotal data from lots of people.
sentences.zh: 我们所拥有的大部分是轶事证据，你可以从很多人那里收集到轶事数据。

sentences.en: Uh, and this has been done, uh, both sort of retrospectively and prospectively.
sentences.zh: 这已经完成了，既有回顾性的，也有前瞻性的。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, there haven't been a lot of well-controlled trials.
sentences.zh: 但是，并没有进行过多少对照良好的试验。

sentences.en: There's only been a few small studies of microdosing and psilocybin and LSD.
sentences.zh: 关于裸盖菇素和LSD的微剂量给药只有几项小规模研究。

sentences.en: Um, they haven't shown anything that to me, uh, shows a clear signal of benefit, uh, more than anything.
sentences.zh: 它们没有显示出任何在我看来能清楚表明其益处的东西，并没有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: What I imagine we're seeing often is, um, some sort of placebo effect where people know they're taking something and they feel like they're feeling better as a result,
sentences.zh: 我想我们经常看到的是某种安慰剂效应，人们知道自己在服用某种东西，结果感觉自己好多了，

sentences.en: whether or not the substance is doing something.
sentences.zh: 无论这种物质是否真的起作用。

sentences.en: Now, I do think that there's a real possibility for microdosing to have therapeutic benefit, but it's really hard and expensive to study it properly,
sentences.zh: 现在，我确实认为微剂量给药有产生治疗益处的可能性，但要正确研究它非常困难且昂贵，

sentences.en: to do a double-blind placebo-controlled study, for instance, in dozens or even, you know, hundreds of people to actually test this out.
sentences.zh: 例如，在几十甚至几百人中进行双盲安慰剂对照研究来实际测试这一点。

sentences.en: And so until that happens, I would say the jury is out, you know, we don't really have a good answer.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之前，我会说结论尚早，我们还没有一个好的答案。

sentences.en: I've certainly spoken to lots of people with very convincing anecdotal reports of getting better from all sorts of different conditions from using microdoses of psilocybin,
sentences.zh: 我当然和很多人谈过，他们有非常令人信服的轶事报告，说通过使用微剂量的裸盖菇素，

sentences.en: for instance.
sentences.zh: 治好了各种不同的疾病。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, nobody's actually drilled down into a cohort of someone, uh, people, for instance, with major depression and studied this carefully.
sentences.zh: 但是，没有人真正深入研究过一个群体，比如重度抑郁症患者，并对此进行仔细研究。

sentences.en: And so until that happens, I think we can't really make a conclusive statement.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之前，我认为我们无法做出结论性的陈述。

sentences.en: Would you say that it's dangerous for people to engage in microdosing?
sentences.zh: 你会说人们进行微剂量给药是危险的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, people are able to get their hands on some of these drugs and, and sort of do it, do it themselves at home.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们能够拿到这些药物，并在家里自己尝试。

sentences.en: I mean, is, is that a good thing?
sentences.zh: 这，这是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I wouldn't advocate for that.
sentences.zh: 我不会提倡这样做。

sentences.en: I mean, it's illegal.
sentences.zh: 这是非法的。

sentences.en: People have lost their jobs, um, you know, for doing that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 人们因为做这种事而丢了工作。

sentences.en: Um, you know, depending on what you're taking, it can be really hard to tell what it is that you have.
sentences.zh: 根据你服用的是什么，很难判断你手里拿到的到底是什么。

sentences.en: If you're talking about, for instance, a synthetic molecule like LSD, you may be getting something very different than what you think you're getting,
sentences.zh: 如果你谈论的是像LSD这样的合成分子，你得到的可能和你认为的完全不同，

sentences.en: which could have, um, significant, uh, adverse health effects.
sentences.zh: 这可能会产生显著的负面健康影响。

sentences.en: Um, with, you know, psilocybin mushrooms, you know, that's something that people can find because they grow out in the world.
sentences.zh: 至于裸盖菇素蘑菇，那是人们可以在野外找到的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, the, the, the only thing I would say there is you may not have the types of mushrooms you think you have.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我唯一想说的是，你手里的蘑菇可能并不是你以为的那种。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, obviously measurement can be difficult, but, um, otherwise I would say that the classic psychedelics,
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，显然剂量控制可能很难，但除此之外，我想说的是，经典的迷幻剂，

sentences.en: if you know what you have and how much you're taking, they're relatively safe for most people.
sentences.zh: 如果你清楚自己拥有的是什么，也知道服用的剂量，那么对于大多数人来说，它们是相对安全的。

sentences.en: Um, and that's, you know, due to the fact that they don't really cause any, um, toxic effects on our major organ systeMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是因为它们实际上不会对我们的主要器官系统造成任何毒性影响。

sentences.en: And so taking small amounts of them shouldn't, uh, be problematic.
sentences.zh: 所以服用少量应该不会有什么问题。

sentences.en: Um, although there, again, a lot of open questions, you know, people have talked about serotonin 2B receptor properties of psilocybin, for instance,
sentences.zh: 嗯，尽管如此，这里仍然有很多未解之谜，比如人们谈论的裸盖菇素对血清素2B受体的作用，

sentences.en: and how that can cause heart valve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 以及这如何可能导致心脏瓣膜问题。

sentences.en: And that actually was related to, uh, medication called fenfen that was being used for weight loss years ago.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与多年前用于减肥的一种名为“芬芬”（fen-phen）的药物有关。

sentences.en: It was pulled from the market because of those same heart valve probleMs.
sentences.zh: 它正是因为同样的心脏瓣膜问题而被撤出市场。

sentences.en: And when you take a psilocybin treatment, for instance, with one high dose, you wouldn't have to worry about that because it's not a chronic dosing regimen.
sentences.zh: 当你进行裸盖菇素治疗时，比如单次高剂量服用，你就不必担心这个问题，因为它不是长期的用药方案。

sentences.en: But if you're taking that often over and over again, um, that does lead to potential, for instance, uh, to develop some of these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但如果你频繁地反复服用，嗯，那确实有可能导致出现其中一些问题。

sentences.en: So again, there's still a lot we don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以再说一次，我们还有很多未知之处。

sentences.en: Um, and so I would certainly, again, not advocate for that type of, uh, treatment, but certainly there's a lot of people who, you know, feel desperate and, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我当然不会提倡那种治疗方式，但确实有很多人，你知道，感到绝望，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: they're looking for something to help them.
sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找能帮助他们的东西。

sentences.en: And, um, I, I can understand that, you know, uh, based on where we're at with, uh, limited treatment options that people are exploring all sorts of different things.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我，我能理解，你知道，考虑到我们目前有限的治疗选择，人们正在探索各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Do you worry that some of these psychedelics are being overhyped or advertised directly to the public?
sentences.zh: 你是否担心其中一些迷幻剂被过度炒作，或者直接向公众进行广告宣传？

sentences.en: For example, there was an opinion piece in the New York times recently headlined, why are ketamine ads following me around the internet?
sentences.zh: 例如，《纽约时报》最近有一篇评论文章，标题是“为什么氯胺酮广告在网上跟踪我？”

sentences.en: And it was about how ketamine is being, um, pushed, you know, by social targeted, social media ads.
sentences.zh: 文章内容是关于氯胺酮是如何通过社交媒体的精准投放广告被推销的。

sentences.en: Is this, is this a problem?
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: Uh, I think it can be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这可能是一个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, just us right now having these conversations, uh, you know, it's likely that we may get one of those ads pop up later on our, on our own social media.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，就在我们现在进行这些对话时，我们之后很可能会在自己的社交媒体上看到其中一个广告弹出。

sentences.en: Um, but, you know, what I, I do think is that there has been, um, a significant overhype of what's going on with the science.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，我确实认为，目前对于科学研究的进展存在着严重的过度炒作。

sentences.en: Um, yes, these drugs seem to have a remarkable therapeutic potentials.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这些药物似乎具有显著的治疗潜力。

sentences.en: And yes, for many years, they've been stigmatized and talked about as, as this sort of, you know, really dangerous drugs of abuse.
sentences.zh: 是的，多年来，它们一直被污名化，被谈论为那种，你知道，非常危险的滥用药物。

sentences.en: Um, but, you know, flipping the script and saying, you know, these are a panacea, um, you know, these are going to save the world, you know, cause,
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，如果反其道而行之，说，你知道，这些是灵丹妙药，嗯，你知道，这些将拯救世界，你知道，因为，

sentences.en: and that was a headline directly pulled from Rolling Stone.
sentences.zh: 这正是《滚石》杂志直接引用的标题。

sentences.en: You know, well, can psychedelics save the world, you know, that, that type of sensationalism, I don't think is helpful, uh, for the general public to be consuming and,
sentences.zh: 你知道，好吧，迷幻剂能拯救世界吗？你知道，那种耸人听闻的报道，我不认为对大众消费有什么帮助，而且，

sentences.en: and particularly for vulnerable populations, including people who are struggling with mental health conditions to, you know, see that type of, uh, media and then, you know,
sentences.zh: 特别是对于弱势群体，包括那些正在与心理健康问题作斗争的人来说，看到那种媒体报道，然后，你知道，

sentences.en: not really know what is the state of the science because, uh, again, often it's overblown.
sentences.zh: 并不真正了解科学的现状，因为，嗯，再说一次，这往往被夸大了。

sentences.en: We know that ketamine has significant, uh, antidepressant effects.
sentences.zh: 我们知道氯胺酮具有显著的抗抑郁作用。

sentences.en: I mean, we've known that for a long time now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们早就知道这一点了。

sentences.en: And so if people can get access to it, um, and they have, uh, you know, serious depression, they can get often relief from that, you know, in a ketamine treatment setting.
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们能够获得它，嗯，而且他们有，嗯，严重的抑郁症，他们通常可以在氯胺酮治疗环境中得到缓解。

sentences.en: Um, but, you know, when you're starting to go out and try to market that or basically sell that to people, uh, aggressively, yeah, I think you definitely,
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，当你开始尝试去营销它，或者基本上是积极地向人们兜售它时，嗯，是的，我认为你绝对，

sentences.en: you're running up against some, um, real potential ethical issues.
sentences.zh: 你正在触碰一些真正的潜在伦理问题。

sentences.en: So what avenues of research are you finding the most exciting right now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你目前觉得哪些研究方向最令人兴奋？

sentences.en: Uh, I'm excited by the, um, prospect of medical approvals by FDA in the next few years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对未来几年FDA批准这些药物的前景感到兴奋，

sentences.en: because I do think that's really going to revolutionize the landscape of mental health care in this country.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实认为这真的会彻底改变这个国家的心理健康护理格局。

sentences.en: Um, I think that that's going to change the model somewhat from what it has been, where we had sort of talk therapy siphoned off on one side, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这将在一定程度上改变过去的那种模式，即谈话疗法被孤立在一边，嗯，

sentences.en: and then pharmacotherapy or medications on the other side.
sentences.zh: 而药物治疗或药物在另一边。

sentences.en: And sometimes people would be doing both, but often not in an integrated fashion.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会同时进行这两种治疗，但往往不是以一种整合的方式。

sentences.en: And what's nice about these treatments is that they bring both together in a comprehensive package and the psychedelic treatments themselves are so different than what's available right now.
sentences.zh: 这些疗法的好处在于，它们将两者结合在一个综合方案中，而且迷幻剂治疗本身与目前可用的疗法截然不同。

sentences.en: And why I say that is because, uh, as we discussed earlier, you know, they really kind of bring you into yourself and what it is, is the root of your issues.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为，嗯，正如我们之前讨论的那样，你知道，它们确实让你深入内心，直面问题的根源。

sentences.en: Um, whether that be relationship problems, um, past trauma, um, you know, issues that you have with self-esteem, um, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，无论是人际关系问题，嗯，过去的创伤，嗯，你知道，你对自己评价的问题，嗯，你知道，

sentences.en: all these different types of things that can be wrapped up in, uh, you know, mental health diagnosis can be sort of unraveled somewhat during the process of this time,
sentences.zh: 所有这些可能被包裹在，嗯，你知道，心理健康诊断中的不同事物，都可以在这个过程中被某种程度上解开，

sentences.en: this kind of psychedelic therapy.
sentences.zh: 这种迷幻疗法。

sentences.en: Um, and then allow people to really resolve them and not just to sort of cover them over with the standard types of, um, therapies that we have available right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后让人们真正解决它们，而不是仅仅用我们目前可用的标准疗法来掩盖它们。

sentences.en: And you can't often do that in talk therapies, obviously over the course of a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 显然，在长期的谈话疗法中，你往往无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: Um, but we, you know, usually we'll have our walls up in our defenses there to try to keep things from changing too fast because that can feel very threatening and scary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，我们通常会竖起心墙和防御机制，试图阻止事情变化得太快，因为那会让人感到非常有威胁和恐惧。

sentences.en: Um, but with psychedelics, it can kind of allow us to make a very deep dive very quickly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但有了迷幻剂，它可以在某种程度上让我们非常迅速地进行深度挖掘。

sentences.en: Um, so I think that's most exciting to me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我认为这对我来说最令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Um, but with the research, you know, you're just seeing more and more, um, research branching out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但随着研究的深入，你知道，你只是看到越来越多的研究在分支扩展。

sentences.en: And so for instance, you know, we're starting to do research now with psilocybin in patients with early stage Alzheimer's disease here.
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道，我们现在开始在这里对早期阿尔茨海默病患者进行裸盖菇素的研究。

sentences.en: Um, my colleague, Dr. Nally Gukassian is working on a nice study that she's just wrapping up in psilocybin in people with anorexia nervosa.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的同事Nally Gukassian博士正在进行一项很好的研究，她即将完成关于裸盖菇素在神经性厌食症患者中的应用研究。

sentences.en: So starting to look at these different areas, um, where we are in clear need of new treatments, uh, and, uh, exploring the potentials there, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以开始关注这些我们显然需要新疗法的不同领域，嗯，并探索那里的潜力，你知道，

sentences.en: I think is also really exciting because it's a new horizon for us.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也非常令人兴奋，因为这对我们来说是一个新的地平线。

sentences.en: Um, we've actually known for a long time that we could use psychedelics to use, uh, to treat addictions, uh, existential distress.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上我们早就知道我们可以使用迷幻剂来治疗成瘾，嗯，存在主义痛苦。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, cause it was being done back in the sixties.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，你知道，因为这在六十年代就已经在做了。

sentences.en: Um, but now we're kind of getting back to the place where we can reestablish that using rigorous and, um, contemporary research methods.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但现在我们正在回到那个位置，我们可以利用严谨的、嗯，当代研究方法重新建立它。

sentences.en: Um, but now there's all these other questions that are on the horizon, including, you know, those new clinical conditions on the one hand.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但现在还有其他所有的问题出现在地平线上，包括，你知道，一方面是那些新的临床病症。

sentences.en: Um, but then also the biological and psychological mechanisms that underlie these drug effects, because it is a mystery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但另一方面也是这些药物作用背后的生物学和心理学机制，因为这确实是一个谜。

sentences.en: You know, we talk about how the brain is reacting to these drugs, um, but it's more than just how is the brain responding.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们谈论大脑如何对这些药物产生反应，嗯，但这不仅仅是大脑如何反应的问题。

sentences.en: It's how is the mind responding, because that's where you start to see changes in the sense of self-identity, for instance, uh,
sentences.zh: 这是心灵如何反应的问题，因为那是你开始看到自我认同感发生变化的地方，例如，嗯，

sentences.en: in a person who's been struggling for years and who identifies as a person with a problem with particular substance, for instance,
sentences.zh: 对于一个多年来一直在挣扎，并且将自己定义为有特定物质问题的人来说，例如，

sentences.en: and is able to change that sense of identity in a way that allows them to live the rest of their lives in a healthier way.
sentences.zh: 并且能够以一种让他们在余生中以更健康的方式生活的方式改变这种认同感。

sentences.en: And so that, you know, I find unique among all the different types of treatments that are out there.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点，你知道，我觉得在所有现有的不同治疗方法中是独一无二的。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Garcia-Romeo, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，Garcia-Romeo博士，我想感谢你今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I think what you're doing is very exciting and we will stay tuned.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所做的事情非常令人兴奋，我们会持续关注。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。
